project: WO-D3 — Worker/provider guide with per-provider limits
description: Publish one canonical packaged `you docs providers` guide that helps operators choose among the configured GPT-5.6 tiers, Claude Sonnet 5, and ANTIGRAVITY models; understand effort, modality, AGY process semantics, and the five-reference ImageGen limit; and use the correct Factory worker frontmatter or ad-hoc `you run` flags. Prove every documented CLI invocation against the current binary and deliver the documentation through merge without adding runtime, provider, CLI, ACP, local-model, multimodal-wrapper, or storage behavior.

context.customerAsk: Publish a canonical packaged worker/provider guide that explains which supported models to choose and why, how reasoning effort is configured, which settings belong in Factory worker frontmatter versus ad-hoc `you run` invocations, and the provider-specific capabilities and limits that operators need before a run. Cover `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `claude-sonnet-5`, ANTIGRAVITY/AGY supported models and efforts, AGY `--add-dir`, print-timeout, and exit-zero-on-decline semantics, `--worker-reasoning-effort`, `--to-file`, the five-path ImageGen `referenced_image_paths` limit, and GPT-5.6's lack of video/audio understanding. Keep canonical content under `docs/reference/`, prove every CLI example against the current binary, run packaged-docs and fast verification, and complete the delivery loop through actual merge.
context.problem: Critical provider behavior is scattered or learned through production failures. Operators exceeded ImageGen's five-reference-path limit and assigned audiovisual judging to GPT-5.6 without knowing it could not see video or hear audio. Model-tier intent, effort vocabulary, Factory versus ad-hoc configuration, and AGY workspace, timeout, and completion semantics are not presented as one decision path, so users can choose an unsuitable provider, misplace a setting, invent a flag, or mistake AGY's zero exit status for task acceptance.
context.solution: Expand the canonical packaged provider topic into an operator-oriented worker/provider guide with a selection matrix, explicit modality and tool limits, configuration ownership, AGY caveats, and copyable Factory and ad-hoc examples. Ground every claim in current worker contracts, provider adapters, recorded AGY evidence, and current-binary CLI behavior; route adjacent reference topics to the canonical guide; and verify the installed `you docs providers` behavior directly without implementing any new runtime capability.

acceptanceCriteria: `you docs providers` presents one coherent selection path covering the intended uses of `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `claude-sonnet-5`, plus ANTIGRAVITY's currently supported AGY models and effort selection, without claiming unverified models or capabilities.

The packaged guide states the known modality and tool constraints before its examples: GPT-5.6 does not provide video/audio understanding, AGY can inspect referenced media through its CLI file-parsing path, and ImageGen accepts at most five `referenced_image_paths` per call.

The guide distinguishes Factory worker frontmatter from ad-hoc `you run` flags, documents `--worker-reasoning-effort` and `--to-file`, and explains AGY's mandatory workspace `--add-dir`, effective `--print-timeout`, and exit-zero-on-decline behavior in terms an operator can act on.

Every CLI invocation printed in changed or new guide content is executed against a binary built from the implementation commit; its real output or a direct behavioral assertion is retained as review evidence, and no example contains an invented flag, model, effort, or output.

Packaged behavior is proven by `make docs-reference-smoke`; the named focused verification command is `go test ./tests/functional/smoke -run '^TestDocsCommandSmoke_' -count=1`, and both commands verify customer-visible `you docs providers` output rather than source inventories or link topology.

Quality gate: Typecheck passes, `make verify-fast` passes, focused docs tests pass, and no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

Delivery continues through implementation and correctness-first review until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, shared-file churn and merge conflicts are reconciled against current main, and the PR is actually merged; opened, green, approved, or ready-to-merge is not complete.

userStories.title: Choose a suitable provider and model before running work
userStories.description: As an operator, I want a provider/model selection guide with explicit capabilities and limits so I can choose a worker that can perceive the input and perform the required task without learning constraints through a failed production run.
acceptanceCriteria: `you docs providers` explains the intended configured roles of `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `claude-sonnet-5`, and separates operator selection guidance from hard provider capability claims.
The guide lists only ANTIGRAVITY models and effort choices supported by current adapter behavior and recorded AGY evidence, and tells readers how AGY is selected through `modelProvider: ANTIGRAVITY`.

A capability/limit table states supported relevant input modalities and the decision consequences, including that GPT-5.6 cannot judge video or audio and AGY is the documented file-parsing route for audiovisual review.

The ImageGen section states that `referenced_image_paths` accepts zero to five paths per call and tells operators to split or redesign work that needs more than five references rather than retrying the same invalid call.

Provider/model names, effort choices, modality statements, and tool limits are checked against current contracts, adapters, and recorded evidence during implementation; uncertain or version-sensitive claims are labeled rather than presented as timeless guarantees.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added the canonical provider/model selection and limits section to docs/reference/providers.md. It distinguishes operator heuristics from adapter facts, covers the configured gpt-5.6-luna/sol/terra and claude-sonnet-5 roles, documents the current AGY model allowlist and model-encoded effort selection, explains modelProvider: ANTIGRAVITY, records GPT-5.6's lack of video/audio understanding versus AGY's recorded workspace file-parsing evidence, and documents ImageGen's 0-5 referenced_image_paths limit with split/redesign guidance. Corrected the guide to state that the public Factory and you run contract rejects a separate AGY reasoning effort, so operators must omit it and select a listed effort-bearing model ID. Removed the stale checked-in-Factory processor claim for gpt-5.6-luna; the current factory assigns processor to CLAUDE/claude-sonnet-5 at high, while gpt-5.6-sol remains the observed planner/ideafier tier. Updated the executable docs smoke assertions. Verified with go test ./tests/functional/smoke -run '^TestDocsCommandSmoke_' -count=1, go test ./pkg/services/providers/... -run 'TestCommandEffect|Test.*Catalog|Test.*Selection' -count=1, make docs-reference-smoke, and make verify-fast (including typecheck, 355 Vitest files/2970 tests, 191 Bun tests, and the short Go suite).

userStories.title: Configure Factory workers and ad-hoc runs on the correct surface
userStories.description: As an operator, I want copyable configuration and invocation examples that distinguish durable worker settings from one-off run flags so I can set effort and pass multiline prompts without misplaced fields or fragile shell quoting.
acceptanceCriteria: The guide includes a clear mapping between canonical Factory worker frontmatter fields (`modelProvider`, `model`, `reasoningEffort`, `skipPermissions`, and applicable timeout settings) and the supported ad-hoc `you run` flags, explicitly including `--worker-reasoning-effort` and `--to-file` without implying every provider-native flag is a `you run` flag.

At least one worker-frontmatter example and one ad-hoc `you run` example show how to select a provider/model and effort, and the multiline example uses `--to-file` so prompt content does not depend on PowerShell argv quoting.

ANTIGRAVITY guidance explains that factory dispatch supplies `agy --add-dir` for the working directory, derives/passes an effective `--print-timeout`, and must interpret the parsed final result because AGY can exit zero after declining the task; operators are not instructed to add provider-native flags to unsupported Factory or `you run` surfaces.

Each CLI invocation shown in the changed guide is executed against the current implementation binary, and review evidence includes the real output or a direct assertion of exit code and relevant output; examples requiring credentials or a provider call use a non-dispatching help/validation path or clearly separate environment-dependent output from deterministic syntax proof.

Invalid or unavailable combinations are described with an actionable alternative, including using AGY for audiovisual inspection, reducing ImageGen references to five or fewer, and omitting a separate effort value where the provider/model contract encodes or rejects it.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added a durable-Factory-versus-ad-hoc mapping to docs/reference/providers.md, including modelProvider/model/reasoningEffort/skipPermissions, timeout ownership, and prompt-file boundaries. Added a valid AGENT_WORKER frontmatter example and a PowerShell-safe --to-file invocation using --provider, --model, and --worker-reasoning-effort. Documented AGY's Factory-owned --add-dir and effective --print-timeout behavior, final-result parsing after exit-zero declines, the public rejection of separate AGY effort, model-ID effort selection, and actionable alternatives for audiovisual work and ImageGen references. Extended the process-boundary docs smoke markers. Rebuilt the current implementation binary and retained direct evidence: run help exposes the documented flags, the exact file-backed shape returns the expected missing-file validation error without dispatch, and an invalid effort returns the pre-dispatch canonical-value diagnostic. Verified with go test ./tests/functional/smoke -run '^TestDocsCommandSmoke_' -count=1, make docs-reference-smoke, focused AGY/worker/CLI tests, and make verify-fast (typecheck, MCP contract check, 355 Vitest files/2970 tests, 191 Bun tests, and the short Go suite).

userStories.title: Deliver the guide through the packaged docs experience

acceptanceCriteria: `you docs providers` from a built CLI outside the repository docs tree prints the complete provider/model, effort, configuration-surface, AGY semantics, modality, and ImageGen limit guidance.

The packaged docs topic index describes `providers` as the canonical worker/provider selection and limits guide, while related `workers`, `run`, and `models` content routes readers to it and does not retain contradictory provider or effort guidance.
Root documentation remains routing/index material; the detailed guide is maintained in canonical `docs/reference/` content and delivered through the existing packaged docs mechanism.

The focused packaged-docs regression proof invokes the docs command and asserts the decision-critical statements visible to customers, including the five-path limit and GPT-5.6 video/audio limitation, without scanning source files or asserting registration inventories.
`make docs-reference-smoke` passes.
The named focused verification command `go test ./tests/functional/smoke -run '^TestDocsCommandSmoke_' -count=1` passes.

Tests pass
